correctness.rationale: The logic normal form is exact on every finite colored graph. In the low regime, the expected number of missing vertex/color incidences is nq(1-p/q)^(n-1)=o(n), giving n-o_p(n) fully saturated vertices, and pigeonhole gives equal depth-one types. In the high regime, conditioning on a same-color pair and multinomial color counts gives an upper bound exp(-2Y) on equal signatures; independent Poissonization yields mean mu=(q-1)(exp(-p lambda)-exp(-p(2-p)lambda)), growing polynomially for alpha>p. Bounded-variable Chernoff and conditioning at mass Theta(n^-1/2) make a fixed-pair collision superpolynomially rare, and a union bound closes the proof. No assertion is made at alpha=p or for unrestricted depth below threshold. Standalone exhaustive small checks corroborate the finite type reduction and first moment.

value.rationale: Sharp and parameter-uniform p-scaled zero-one threshold for one-step distinguishability on a foundational stochastic Kripke model. It is a natural expressive-power question with independent sample valuations, combines exact occupancy first moments with Poisson concentration, exposes a non-obvious effect of random color-class sizes, and is not an arbitrary finite slice or known table recomputation.
